News.title: Family of pregnant Brit found dead in hotel after marrying Ghanaian ‘prophet’ demand answers over her ‘mystery’ death
News.content:
SHE was a bubbly “social butterfly” who thought she had finally found her “man of God”.

Charmain Speirs, a devout Christian and expectant mother, thought her prayers had been answered when she was swept off her feet by a charismatic celebrity preacher nicknamed “The Prophet”.





Charmain Spiers, 40, met Ghanaian preacher Eric Adusah in 2014 through an online dating site, and they married after a whirlwind romance.

But just six months after their wedding, the 40-year-old was found dead in a hotel bathtub in Ghana, 5,000 miles from her home in Arbroath.

Local police arrested Adusah on suspicion of murder but the case was dropped due to lack of evidence.

He has always denied any involvement in Charmain’s death.

A post-mortem in Ghana gave her cause of death as a heroin overdose, and a UK inquest later recorded an open conclusion.

Recording her cause of death as opiate poisoning, Home Office pathologist Charlotte Randall said: “We shall never quite know what happened.

“There just isn’t the evidence.”

Charmain’s family are however desperate for answers as to what happened in room 112 10 years on since her death.



Her devastated loved ones insist she would never touch the drug that had already ravaged her family.

And her death is now subject to a major three-part documentary, Charmain and the Prophet, which is now available on BBC iPlayer.

Speaking in the TV show, Charmain’s mum Linda said: “She hated anybody on drugs.

“She just couldn’t stand it. She says: ‘why would anybody do that to their body’.”

And her son Isaac, born from a previous relationship, also is demanding answers over his mum’s death.



He said: “I have to live the rest of my life knowing that my mum is never going to see what I do in my life.

“It really gets to me.”

Her family and friends insist she was not a drug user – with the inquest finding no evidence of long-term opiod abuse – and she was not suicidal.

The so-called “prophet” Adusah, now lives in the United States under the name Eric Isaiah Kusi Boateng – and he declined to answer questions to the BBC.

Growing up on Scotland’s east coast in the 1970s and 80s, Charmain was the girl everyone wanted to be around.



Her mother Linda, a cleaner, and her father Peter, a plumber, watched as their daughter became the heart of every room she entered.

Friends described her as a “social butterfly” who people gravitated towards – but life wasn’t always kind.

The family endured the agony of losing one son in a car crash, while Charmain’s youngest brother succumbed to the grip of heroin addiction – a tragedy that friends say left her with a lifelong, visceral hatred of drugs.

In her early thirties, seeking a fresh start, Charmain moved to Swansea to study photojournalism.

It was there, as a single mother to her son Isaac, that she battled post-natal depression and found solace in the fast-growing world of Pentecostalism.



Through her faith, she appeared to find the happiness that had eluded her, but she still felt a void.

Her friend Anne-Marie recalls that Charmain had simply “had enough of normal men” and felt she had been promised a partner who shared her spiritual intensity.

That man appeared in the spring of 2014.

Eric Adusah was the head pastor of the Global Light Revival Church, a high-profile preacher who appeared regularly on Christian television.



After meeting on a Christian dating site, the pair embarked on a lightning-fast courtship and within weeks, an engagement was announced.

Her mother, Linda, was stunned to hear her daughter was getting married before she’d even known there was a boyfriend in the picture.

Bridesmaid Mehrunissa Thomas remembers the sudden shift in status, noting that Charmain had gone from being a normal person to a bona fide celebrity in the eyes of the church.

Son’s horror

To her congregation, she was the “First Lady” – the wife of a man they called a Prophet, a figure believed to receive divine revelations directly from the Almighty.

But as Charmain embraced her new life in London under her new moniker, the reality behind closed doors was far from the blessed union she had envisioned.



Friends noticed a change as the woman who was once a daily fixture in their lives began to vanish from view.

She confided to pals that there was no love or passion in the marriage, describing a coldness that stood in stark contrast to Adusah’s fiery public persona.

In the documentary Isaac claims his mother would stand between him and Adusah to protect him from the preacher’s rage

Isaac’s memories are not of a holy man, but one he accuses of being controlling and manipulative.

He added: “The way he talked to my mum, the way he treated her, he wasn’t a prophet. He was an evil human being.



“He didn’t deserve a fraction of the praise he got in that church”

Fatal trip to Ghana

Despite the apparent cracks in the marriage, Charmain – now pregnant with Adusah’s child – stayed.

But by early 2015, she was reaching her breaking point.

During a visit to Arbroath, she told her mother the marriage was on the rocks and she intended to move back home to Scotland.

It was the last time Linda would see her daughter alive.



Charmain and Adusah flew to Ghana and it was in the city of Koforidua that the tragedy unfolded.

According to police statements, Adusah was the last person to see his wife alive.

He told investigators they had spent a pleasant day together, eating lunch and visiting the hotel pool, before returning to room 112 for the night.

Adusah claimed he left the hotel shortly after midnight to travel to Accra for a meeting, leaving Charmain behind because she wanted to extend her stay.

When she was found dead in the bathtub days later, Adusah was arrested on suspicion of murder – but then released without charge.



Heroin mystery

The most “insulting” part of the case for Charmain’s family was the claim that she died of a drug overdose.

Adusah had told police his wife was suicidal and had a history of drug abuse.

However, the hotel room contained no drugs, needles or paraphernalia.

Charmain’s loved ones are adamant she would never have used heroin, especially while pregnant.

“She hated anybody on drugs,” Linda told the BBC, recalling how her daughter was repulsed by the habit after seeing what it did to her brother.



The truth about what happened in room 112 may never be known – but her family will never stop fighting for answers.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source close to Adusah told The Sun he handed himself into the police after Charmain’s death to get “the truth”.

He insisted he was only then detained because he was the “last person to see her alive”, adding that he arranged for her body to be brought back to the UK himself “for further investigation”.

News.title: Pedestrian, 44, killed in early hours hit-and-run as cops hunt driver who fled
News.content:
HIT-AND-RUN DEATH Pedestrian, 44, killed in early hours hit-and-run as cops hunt driver who fled

A MAN has tragically died after a horror hit-and-run in the early hours – as cops hunt the driver.

An investigation has been launched after Shaun Harron, 44, was fatally struck in Birmingham, West Midlands, just after 12.30am today.



Shaun was hit by a brown Vauxhall Astra on the junction of Romsley Road and Adams Hill in Bartley Green.

The vehicle – which had the registration LV63 WHN – did not stop and fled the scene towards Jiggins Lane.



West Midlands Police said paramedics treated Shaun for his injuries before rushing him to hospital.

However, despite the best efforts of medical teams, he was pronounced dead a short while later.

Officers are now scouring CCTV and conducting door-to-door enquiries as a probe remains ongoing into the horror.

Sgt Rich Evans, from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit, urged anyone with more information or footage of the hit-and-run to get in touch.



He said: “Tragically Shaun Harron has lost his life after being struck by a car which did not then stop.

“Our thoughts are with his loved ones at this terrible time.

“Investigators are working at pace to trace the vehicle and believe it will have sustained damage in the incident.

“If anyone can help, we’d urge them to get in touch.



“We’d also ask anyone who was in the area or may have dashcam footage as they drove through at around the time of the collision to get in touch.”

It comes as cops confirmed a teen boy tragically died in a head-on crash between a van and a motorcycle.

The horror collision took place near Sittingbourne, Kent, just before 5pm on Saturday, police said.

A 17-year-old boy, who was riding a black KTM Duke motorcycle, was travelling in Tonge when it collided with a blue VW Transporter van.

Despite the best efforts of paramedics, he was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.



Kent Police is now urgently appealing for witnesses and anyone who may have dash-cam footage of the incident.

News.title: Trump ‘likely target’ of White House dinner shooting as teacher suspect, 31, lay in wait at hotel ‘with guns and knives’
News.content:
PRESIDENT Donald Trump was most likely the target of the White House Correspondents dinner shooting, authorities have said.

The suspected gunman Cole Tomas Allen, 31, was allegedly lying in wait inside the Washington Hilton Hotel to target Trump administration officials.





“It does appear that ⁠he did, ⁠in fact, set ‌out to target folks that work ‌in the administration, likely including the president,” Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

Allen was allegedly armed with a shotgun, handgun, and knives when he charged a security checkpoint outside the packed black-tie gala which was being held in the ballroom of the venue.

President Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, Vice President JD Vance, as well as other senior government officials and journalists were all inside.

Officials believe Allen had checked into the hotel where the black-tie dinner was being held.

Investigators believe Allen traveled by train from California to Chicago before heading to Washington, DC.



He is accused of smuggling weapons inside the hotel after paying for a room.

A volunteer told The Post they saw him assemble a long weapon “in [an] unsecured room.”

Moments later, Allen allegedly dashed the ballroom where Trump, Melania Trump, Vice President JD Vance, cabinet members, and journalists were gathered.

The president and first lady had made their grand entrance onto the dais about 20 minutes before the shooting.



Secret Service agents rushed Trump and Melania away as guests ducked under tables.

Panicked attendees were heard screaming “get down, get down!” as officers flooded the room.

Trump later posted CCTV footage on Truth Social that appeared to show the suspect sprinting through a security cordon.

Two Secret Service agents could be seen pulling out their guns before more officers swarmed the area.

A Secret Service agent was shot in the vest during the gunfight.



Trump said the agent was taken to hospital and was in “great spirits.”

FBI officials later said the suspect opened fire at the agent.

Secret Service Deputy Director Matthew Quinn said Allen tried to cause a “national tragedy.”

“[Allen] underestimated the protective capabilities of the U.S. Secret Service, and was stopped at first contact,” Quinn said.

“The strength of our layered security posture was evident, with a myriad of countermeasures ahead.”



Authorities said they seized a shotgun, a handgun, and multiple knives when Allen was arrested.

He was taken from the hotel in the back of an ambulance.

Allen has been charged with using a firearm during a crime of violence and assaulting a federal officer, US Attorney Jeanine Pirro said.

Officials have not revealed a motive.

Trump said he did not believe the attack was linked to the ongoing US-Israeli war in Iran.



“It’s not going to deter me from winning the war in Iran,” Trump told reporters.

“I don’t know if that had anything to do with it. I really don’t think so, based on what we know.”

Trump described Allen as a “would-be assassin” and a “lone wolf whack job” from California.

He also called him a “sick person.”

Allen has been described as a CalTech-educated teacher from Torrance, California.



A LinkedIn profile matching his name and photo says he worked as a part-time teacher at C2 Education.

The profile says he graduated from the California Institute of Technology in 2017 with a mechanical engineering degree.

It also says he earned a master’s degree in computer science from California State University-Dominguez Hills last year.

Allen described himself online as a “mechanical engineer and computer scientist by degree, independent game developer by experience, teacher by birth.”

He also appears to have published an indie game called Bohrdom on Steam for $1.99.



A former high school volleyball teammate told NBC News Allen was a “borderline genius” and “super stable.”

FBI agents later raided a home in Torrance linked to Allen.

Pictures from the scene showed armored vehicles, police tape, and heavily armed officers outside the property.

A neighbor told CNN they were unsure whether Allen lived there because they rarely saw him.

But the neighbor said they had seen him “a couple of days ago.”



Torrance Mayor George Chen said reports linking the suspect to the city were “deeply troubling.”

“While that connection is deeply troubling, one individual’s actions do not define our city,” Chen said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump said the White House Correspondents’ Dinner will be rescheduled within the next 30 days.

The Washington Hilton is the same hotel where president Ronald Reagan survived an assassination attempt 45 years earlier – he was shot and seriously wounded after a speaking engagement in 1981.

News.title: Why your dog walk is suddenly taking twice as long as usual – ‘spring fever’ could be to blame
News.content:
DOG owners may notice their walks taking longer now that spring is here.

While this may seem like a random occurrence, there is actually a reason behind it.



While your pooch may power through a walk with minimal distractions during winter, the spring season offers more temptation for them to stop and sniff.



Canine experts have revealed this change in behaviour is largely driven by the increase in smells during this time of year.

With a dog’s sense of smell estimated to be tens of thousands of times stronger than a human’s, your regular walking route can provide a wide variety of scents each time you go out.

And while cold winter temperatures mean reduced wildlife activity, spring brings more animals outdoors, increasing scent trails.

Blooming plants also begin releasing stronger smells, creating a “sensory explosion” for your furry friend.



Jo Hinds, certified behaviourist and dynamic dog practitioner at dog food subscription service Years, spoke to the Daily Mail about this “spring fever” phenomenon.

“In spring, the environment becomes much richer in scents from plants, wildlife and other animals,” she explained.

“For dogs, this creates a huge amount of new information to explore.”

The canine pro continued: “Sniffing allows them to gather information about other animals, territory and their surroundings, which is why walks can become much slower during this time of year.”



And since your pooch can benefit from this, you should avoid rushing them or pulling on the lead while they’re having a good sniff.

“Sniffing is actually an important form of mental stimulation for dogs,” Hinds said.

“Allowing sniffing during walks can actually help with emotional regulation, when they are relaxed in their environment, which can reduce pulling and provide enrichment.

“Spring is an exciting time for dogs because their world suddenly becomes full of new smells.”

News.title: Moment Hollywood VIP casually eats his dinner as dozens around him hide under tables and flee during Washington shooting
News.content:
THIS is the bizarre moment a Hollywood agent casually eats his dinner as chaos erupts around him after gunshots were fired during a White House dinner.

Hundreds of journalists and media bigwigs were enjoying the prestigious yearly gala at the Hilton Hotel in Washington when a gunman stormed security outside the ballroom.





An odd video captured in the moments after President Donald Trump was ushered out of the room by Secret Service agents has since gone viral for one VIP guest’s peculiar response.

A tuxedo-ed man, later identified as talent agent Michael Glantz, can be seen calmly reaching his fork over to his plate as he tucks into his meal.

As attendees dove for cover under their white-clothed tables, Glantz peacefully filled his belly.

The White House Correspondents’ Dinner had just served first course — a burrata and fresh‑pea salad — when Cole Tomas Allen, 31, allegedly opened fire in the lobby after sprinting past secret service agents.

Allen is facing firearms and assault charges after he was arrested in Washington over the terrifying shooting.

Members of global media outlets, including The Sun’s Editor-at-Large Harry Cole, pulled out their phones and began recording reports of the alleged assassination attempt.

Glantz, a super-agent for Creative Artists Agency (CAA) which represents media stars including past President Joe Biden, seemed unfazed by the potential danger around him.



The video of Glantz has since gone viral on social media, with commentators finding his actions down-right ridiculous.

In an interesting twist, the same hotel served as the stage for the 1981 assassination attempt of then-President Ronald Reagan.

Diners were expecting a main course of filet mignon and lobster, followed by a decadent selection of desserts.

Immediately after the alleged attack, Trump posted on Truth Social that he had recommended that the “show go on”.

About 20 minutes later, the president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, Weijia Jiang, announced that the party would resume “as soon as possible.”



Guests had begun to leave at that point and many reporters met up again later at the briefing room at the White House for a hastily arranged press conference.

Trump bravely addressed the world just an hour after the shooting.

He said: “It’s always shocking when something like this happens.”



“The fact that we were sitting next to each other, the First Lady on my right, and I heard a noise.”

The US president added that at first he thought it was a tray being dropped on the floor by a staff member.

Melania was the first to raise the alarm that the sound could be gunfire, Trump added.

She was seen looking around in horror, her face frozen in worry.

The First Lady told her husband about the “bad noise”, as Trump added that “it was a rather traumatic experience for her”.



“Melania was very cognisant,” he continued.

“The First Lady was doing a terrific job. She loves the country.



“She recognises it better than any. But she told me numerous times, she said ‘you are in a dangerous job’.”

Officials said the suspected shooter had no criminal record but that he was armed with a shotgun, a handgun and multiple knives.

Dramatic footage shows agents pinning the suspected shooter to the ground.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Video shows the suspected shooter lying face down outside the Washington Hilton with his hands tied behind his back covered in a foil blanket.

Overnight, heavily armed agents swarmed a home in Torrance, California, linked to Allen, who is understood to be a teacher.

News.title: Distraught Erika Kirk hides under table & sobs ‘I want to go home’ as she flees dinner months after husband’s murder
News.content:
HEARTBREAKING footage shows the moment a distraught Erika Kirk was left sobbing as she fled the shooting at the White House Correspondents Dinner.

The mom-of-two was left visibly shaken and sobbing as she was ushered out of the venue saying, “I just want to go home.”





Gunfire erupted at the Washington Hilton hotel just seven months after her husband, Charlie Kirk, was assassinated at a student event in Utah in September.

Several shots sounded and the widow, who was in attendance as a guest of Fox News dove underneath a table for safety.

She had been sitting alongside Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard and Fox News’ Lawrence Jones.

Shooting suspect Cole Tomas Allen, 31, was arrested at the scene and is set to be charges with firearms and assault offenses and officials believe he was targeting members of the Trump Administration.



One Secret Service agent was shot and taken to hospital but has since been released.

No one else is believed to have been injured in the terrifying incident where senior government officials and correspondents had gathered.

Just weeks ago, Kirk, who took over from her late-husband as the CEO of Turning Point USA, backed out of appearing next to Vice President JD Vance at the University of Georgia over safety fears.



Vance still attended the TPUSA event despite what organizers called “very serious threats” against Kirk.

“I was so looking forward to tonight’s event at the @universityofga with our Vice President @JDVance, but after all our family has been through, I take my security team’s recommendations extremely seriously,” she wrote.

“Thank you to our amazing Georgia chapter for your support. God bless you all!”

It comes as…

The suspected shooter Cole Tomas Allen has been arrested

Trump posted chilling footage of the “gunman” charging the venue

The FBI raid home of shooter

Dramatic video shows how Melania bravely alerted Trump

The Sun’s Harry Cole reveals how he was just feet away from the chaos

Kirk is yet to publicly comment on the Washington dinner shooting.



On Sunday, Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said it is believed that Allen, tried to breach the ballroom in a pre-planned attack targeting members of the Trump administration.

“It does appear ​that ⁠he did, ⁠in fact, set ‌out to target folks that work ‌in the administration, likely including the president,” he said.

The 31-year-old remains in custody and facing multiple charges.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This is not the first time in the past couple of years that our Republic has been attacked by a would-be assassin who sought to kill,” President Trump said in a briefing after the incident.

“In light of this evening’s events, I ask that all Americans recommit with their hearts in resolving our differences peacefully.”

News.title: Who is Cole Tomas Allen? What we know about alleged suspect in White House correspondents’ dinner shooting
News.content:
What we know about the alleged suspect who opened fire at the White House correspondents' dinner on Saturday night.

SUSPECT ARRESTED Who is Cole Tomas Allen? What we know about alleged suspect in White House correspondents’ dinner shooting

Credit: Alamy Live News.

THE world was shook on Saturday evening after a suspect allegedly stormed the White House Correspondents’ dinner and opened fire at the event attended by US President Donald Trump.

Trump and his wife, First Lady Melania – who turns 56 on Sunday – were rushed away from the event by Secret Service agents.



Meanwhile, other guests in attendance at the Washington Hilton scampered to hide under tables after an individual charged a security checkpoint and injured a law enforcement officer.

The individual in question was later identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, from Torrance, California.



Read on below for everything you need to know about Allen following the incident and his subsequent arrest.

Who is Cole Tomas Allen?

Allen resides in Torrance, California, located along Santa Monica Bay near Los Angeles.

CBS have reported that the alleged shooter told authorities he was planning to target Donald Trump.

Allen reportedly worked as a tutor in Torrance after graduating from the California Institute of Technology.



The chief of Washington DC’s police department revealed that investigators believe Allen was staying at the Washington Hilton, where Trump was in attendance for the Correspondents’ dinner.

Federal campaign finance records also reveal that Allen contributed $25 to a Democratic Party political action committee in endorsement of Kamala Harris.

That payment was made during her 2024 presidential campaign, which ultimately saw her lose out to Trump, who was elected for a second term.

The 31-year-old had no criminal record but was armed with a shotgun, a handgun and multiple knives, according to officials.



What has Donald Trump said about the White House shooting?

Trump subsequently addressed the world in a news conference at the White House just an hour after the shooting took place.

The US President said that Allen would be “spending life in prison”, adding: “He’s in custody and they’re asking him a lot of questions.”

He said: “It’s always shocking when something like this happens.”

“The fact that we were sitting next to each other, the First Lady on my right, and I heard a noise.”



The US president added that at first he thought it was a tray being dropped on the floor by a staff member.

Jeanine Pirro, the US attorney for Washington, said the suspect was facing two counts for using firearm during crime of violence and assault on federal officers using dangerous weapon.

She added that he would be arraigned on Monday and be formally charged in federal court.

News.title: Charlie Kirk's widow Erika sobs as she's rushed to safety from White House Correspondents' dinner shooting
News.content:
Charlie Kirk's widow Erika sobs as she's rushed to safety from White House Correspondents' dinner shooting

Erika Kirk was seen weeping as she was rushed out of the White House correspondents' dinner and said five words while quickly leaving the scene after a gunman stormed the event

Erica Kirk in tears after shooting at Trump dinner

Charlie Kirk's distraught widow Erika was seen sobbing as she was rushed out of the White House correspondents' dinner to safety after a gunman opened fire.

‌



The annual event was plunged into chaos when gunshots sent 2,500 guests in a ballroom at the Washington Hilton hotel ducking for cover under tables while Donald Trump was quickly evacuated. Erika Kirk, Charlie Kirk's widow, was among the first people to be moved out of the room late on Saturday night, soon after the President and First Lady were rushed out by the Secret Service.

The CEO of the right-wing political charity Turning Point USA was caught weeping as she was evacuated and said "I just want to go home" as she walked past a camera.

View 5 Images Erika Kirk crying as she is led away from the attack (Image: instagram/@sarasidnertv)

The suspect in the shooting attack was named as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, from California. Police said the suspect was armed with multiple weapons including a shotgun, handgun and multiple knives.

This incident came just over six months since Charlie Kirk was shot in the neck and killed while speaking at a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University. After Charlie's death, Erika, 37, took over as head of Turning Point USA and has become the face of the right-wing group.

View 5 Images Erika Kirk said 'I just want to go home' (Image: instagram/@sarasidnertv)

A sponsor of the group, Derek Myers, later posted: "Erika is okay but very upset. She was crying." The widow had been seen, in photos from earlier that night, at the dinner sat next to the controversial US Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard.

Erika had been a guest of Fox News at the annual dinner. Eyewitness reports claimed Erika initially hid under a table before she was promptly ushered out.

It was also claimed the widow was crying and consoled by FBI director Kash Patel, according to People. This comes after Erika Kirk last week pulled out of a Turning Point USA event, in Athens, Georgia, with Vice President JD Vance.

View 5 Images Erika Kirk with Donald Trump at a memorial for Charlie Kirk (Image: AP)

The CEO said she did this because she was "worried" and "some threats". The 37-year-old received "some very serious threats in her direction" a spokesperson for the right-wing charity told Fox News.

Vance said "I know that she did get some threats" before adding: "She was very worried about it." Shocking CCTV footage from Washington Hilton hotel, last night, showed the suspect running through a security checkpoint and towards the ballroom.

View 5 Images Cole Tomas Allen was arrested (Image: @REALDONALDTRUMP / TRUTH SOCIAL/AFP via Getty Images)

The President was not injured in the attack but one Secret Service member was shot at by the suspect but their bulletproof vest saved them, officials said. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said that the accused gunman is believed to have been targeting Donald Trump and members of his administration.

He added that officials also believe the suspect had travelled by train from California to Chicago and then onto Washington where he checked in as a guest to the hotel where the event was being held. Law enforcement officials who have examined his electronic devices and writings preliminarily believe he intended to target administration members attending the dinner.

Article continues below

View 5 Images The suspect running past a security checkpoint at the hotel (Image: TRUTH SOCIAL)

“It does appear that he did in fact set out to target folks who work in the administration, likely including the president,” Blanche told NBC’s 'Meet the Press'. The US Attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, said the suspected is expected to appeared in court on Monday and be formally charged with several offences, including using a firearm during a crime of violence.

This has been the third time since 2024 that the US President had been under threat by an attacker in his immediate vicinity – including the assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, that injured him and killed a local firefighter.

News.title: Sir Ken Dodd's catchphrases are trademarked eight years after his death
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Sir Ken Dodd's catchphrases are trademarked eight years after his death

It's tattyfilarious as Sir Ken Dodd's unique brand of humour is set for a comeback.

Lady Anne Dodd chats about The Ken Dodd Charitable Foundation

The catchphrases of comedy icon Sir Ken Dodd could soon be tickling audiences again, eight years after his death. His widow Lady Anne, 84, has filed a raft of papers with a government body to trademark Doddy's name and unique brand of humour in TV and film.

‌



The application includes old favourites such as tattyfilarious, Tickling Stick, How Tickled I am and Discomknockerated. His Diddymen and Knotty Ash birthplace will also be trademarked.

‌



The firm, Knotty Ash Productions Ltd, has applied to the UK’s Intellectual Property Office to protect 25 of his famous slogans. Jam Butty Mines, Treacle Wills, and Broken Biscuit Repair Factory are all on the list.

‌



View 3 Images The late Sir Ken Dodd with his famous tickling sticks (Image: Peter Rogan)

13 Man Utd players who could be moved on in savage summer clear-out READ MORE :

The application covers use in entertainment, theatre productions, TV programming, presentations, festivals, DVD TV and film production, documentaries, and comedy shows.

The much-loved comic married Anne, his partner of 40 years, just two days before he died at the age of 90 in March 2018. He was still working just months before his death.

‌



View 3 Images Lady Anne Dodd (Image: Andy Stenning/Daily Mirror)

He was revered in his home city, Liverpool, where he was born the son of a coal merchant in 1927. Dad Arthur bought him a Punch and Judy set for his 8th birthday. Young Ken was soon charging school friends twopence to watch the puppets. He left school at 14 and worked with his brother Bill in their father's business. But in his spare time, the former choirboy sang and worked as a stand-up comedian at working men's clubs, with material scripted by his father.

He was billed as "Professor Yaffle Chucklebutty. Operatic Tenor and Sausage Knotter". The Theatre Royal in Nottingham hosted his professional debut in 1954, where he earned £75 a week as Professor Chucklebutty. Dodd later joked: "At least they didn't boo me off".

‌



View 3 Images Ken Dodd's life was celebrated in an exhibition (Image: Colin Lane/Liverpool Echo)

Within two years he was topping the bill at Blackpool. In the 1960s he made it into the Guinness Book of Records for telling 1,500 jokes in three and a half hours. After making his name in the music halls, his TV and radio career took off. He was also a chart-topping singer: his signature tune, "Happiness," was released in 1964. His single, "Tears," was the third highest-selling song of the 1960s in Britain, beaten only by two Beatles singles.

Sir Ken met Anne when she appeared in the Ken Dodd Christmas Show at the Manchester Opera House in 1961. Throughout the 1970s and 80s, he was a regular on TV, working to a punishing schedule and seldom taking a holiday.

Article continues below

In 1989, Sir Ken was charged with eight counts of tax fraud spanning 15 years and involving more than £800,000. He was acquitted after the court heard a range of stories about his eccentricity, including hiding more than £300,000 in wardrobes, cupboards and under the stairs.

After his acquittal, Sir Ken resumed his career, enjoying another season at the London Palladium in 1990. He also won a British Comedy Lifetime Achievement Award and was voted Top Variety Performer in 1993.

News.title: Calls for Keir Starmer to face sleaze inquiry over Mandelson branded 'political games'
News.content:
Calls for Keir Starmer to face sleaze inquiry over Mandelson branded 'political games'

The Tories are pressing for a vote on whether to refer Keir Starmer to the Privileges Committee over whether he misled Parliament over Peter Mandelson's appointment as US ambassador

View 2 Images Keir Starmer is under unrelenting pressure over his decision to send Peter Mandelson to Washington (Image: AP)

Attempts to refer Keir Starmer to a sleaze inquiry over the Peter Mandelson vetting row have been dismissed as “political games”.

‌



The Tories are pressing Commons Speaker Sir Lindsay Hoyle to give MPs a vote on whether to refer the Prime Minister to the powerful Privileges Committee over whether he misled Parliament over the peer's appointment as US ambassador.

‌



The committee previously found Boris Johnson misled Parliament over Partygate and handed him a 90-day suspension. The ex-PM quit as an MP in a fury before the punishment could be imposed.

‌



The Speaker is expected to give a statement to MPs as soon as Monday. While a vote would be unlikely to pass due to Labour’s huge majority, it would pile further pressure on the PM. His judgement has been called into question after the former Labour grandee was sent to Washington despite vetting officials flagging concerns about his vetting.

Dominic Grieve, a former Tory attorney general, said: “Seeing that this appointment is being explored during these processes and all the evidence is not yet considered, it is impossible to see how starting a reference to the Privileges Committee is either useful or indeed ‘due process’.

OPINION Dave Burke Keir Starmer stumbles through Peter Mandelson crisis - but next week could be worse

‌



Keir Starmer’s former top aide urged to hire lawyers before facing MPs by Tom Watson READ MORE :

View 2 Images Sir Lindsay Hoyle is being lobbied by MPs to allow a vote on whether to refer Keir Starmer to the powerful Privileges Committee (Image: PA)

"Ensuring that ministers do not mislead Parliament is of great importance but it should not just be turned into political games.”

Harriet Harman, who led the Privileges Committee investigation into Mr Johnson, also advised against the idea. She told LBC: “I don't... It would be complete duplication. At the moment, there is an investigation going on by the Foreign Affairs Select Committee, so I think it would be a duplication.

‌



"I would say, leave them to sort this out. And of course, we've got further tranches of documents to come out into the public domain, because that's the motion of the House of Commons that's been passed.”

Baroness Harman said the PM was right to apologise for appointing Lord Mandelson - and said Mr Starmer's decision to sack Foreign Office boss Sir Olly Robbins had made things worse. "He should just stay with 'it's a bad decision'," she said.

Cabinet Minister Darren Jones said “there is no case to answer” for the PM as Sir Olly had been clear that he did not tell Mr Starmer about concerns over Lord Mandelson's vetting before he was sent to Washington.

‌



He said: “You have to remember, what are these privileges committees about? The last time it was used was when Boris Johnson told the House of Commons there were no parties in Downing Street.

“It was then shown he was at five of them and got a fine from the police. That’s what these processes are in place for, so the Opposition are just using tactics to try to distract from the fact that the Government is doing good work in this pre-election period.”

A No10 source said: “The Tories are trying to pull off a ridiculous and baseless political stunt the week before the May elections – because they have no answers on the cost of living or the NHS.”

Article continues below

The PM's nightmare over Lord Mandelson's vetting will continue this week as MPs prepare to grill Morgan McSweeney, the former No10 chief of staff, and ex-Foreign Office boss Sir Philip Barton on Tuesday.

As questions mount over his leadership, Mr Starmer insisted the "vast majority" of Labour MPs support him and want him to continue as PM. In an interview with the Sunday Times, he said: "What you never hear from are all the people who are supportive, loyal and just want to get on with the job. And that is the vast majority of people in the Parliamentary Labour Party."

He added: "They're pleased to be in power. They've waited a long time to be in power. And they just want to get on with their job. They don't make a lot of noise about it. They don't talk to journalists about it. It's really important that is reflected in these debates."

News.title: Donald Trump assassination attempts in full after gunman storms White House Correspondents' Dinner
News.content:
Donald Trump assassination attempts in full after gunman storms White House Correspondents' Dinner

Gunmen have been close to shooting President Trump at a golf course, a public rally and now a hotel after a man opened fire at the White House Correspondents' Dinner last night

View 6 Images President Trump describes the gunman as 'sick' in a press conference after the shooting attempt (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

President Trump has now survived three potential assassination attempts in just 21 months having been at the centre of numerous security scares.

‌



He has been targeted at a rally, a golf course and now a hotel, surviving each attempt. But the latest shooting attempt was described as an "historic security failure". A man armed with guns and knives stormed the lobby of the Washington Hilton last night during the annual White House Correspondents' Association Dinner.

‌



Footage showed him running through a metal detector and rushing security as he charged toward the ballroom in what a security expert said could have been a "catastrophe". One officer was shot, with the bullet hitting his bullet-resistant vest. Trump and other top US politicians were rushed off stage and out of the event while the gunman was tackled to the ground and taken into custody.

‌



View 6 Images Trump was escorted off stage after the gunman opened fire (Image: REUTERS)

Andrew Badger, former defence intelligence agency officer, told Sky News: "I think this is a historic event. What strikes me is that eight out of the nine cabinet members who would succeed President Trump were at this single event...this is a historic failure, this gunman should never have got that close to the President."

Trump came the closes to being assassinated in July 13 2024, when a bullet grazed his right ear. Thomas Matthew Crooks, 20, fired eight times with a rifle from a roof overlooking the Trump rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. He failed to assassinate Trump but killed another attendee Corey Comperatore, 50, a former volunteer fire chief who was in the crowd and shielding his family. Two others were seriously injured. The gunman was killed by a Secret Service sniper.

‌



View 6 Images Donald Trump, a bandage on his ear after he was injured during an assassination attempt, in 2024 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

In the seconds after being shot, a defiant President Trump stood up with blood on his face and raised his right fist shouting ‘fight, fight, fight’. A subsequent senate report criticised Secret Service planning, communications and leadership. They were slammed for allowing the gunman to breach the security perimeter with a rifle and reach an elevated position close to Trump.

‌



Video of the attack and the accounts of eyewitnesses suggest that members of the crowd became aware of the threat before the police and other security officials and attempted to alert them to the danger. But it was only when the gunman opened fire that officials recognised the danger and responded, with Thomas Crooks shot dead by armed officers.

View 6 Images Trump reacts after an assassination attempt in July 2024 (Image: AP)

‌



Then in September 2024, West Palm Beach, Florida, a gunman was spotted with a rifle at Trump’s International Golf Club while the President was playing on the course. Just as Trump moved holes, a Secret Service agent spotted a muzzle peeking out from the bushes. A Secret Service agent fired at Ryan Wesley Routh, 58, who fled without firing a shot and was arrested on a nearby highway. He is now serving a life sentence.

In September 2025, a New York (NYPD) off duty police officer, Melvin Eng, turned up at the Ryder Cup golf tournament at Bethpage Black Course in New York, armed and in full tactical gear, pretending to be part of Trump’s security detail. It was later discovered that Eng was on sick leave, had no official assignment to be part of the president’s detail and no assigned role at the event. The incident reportedly led to Eng’s suspension, pending further investigation by the NYPD.

View 6 Images Secret Service surround Trump as a gunman opens fire at a rally from a rooftop overlooking the event in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



In February this year, US Secret Service agents and a deputy from the Palm Beach County Sheriff's office shot and killed an armed man who entered the inner perimeter at Mar-a-Lago, President Trump’s residence in Florida. He was not there at the time of the incident. The suspect 21-year-old Austin T. Martin, from North Carolina, was reportedly carrying a shotgun and a fuel cannister when he entered Mar-a-Lago. TMZ later reported that Martin had grown increasingly obsessed with Epstein, a former friend of Trump.

The latest shooting took place in the same hotel where former President Reagan was wounded by John Hinckley Jr. on March 30, 1981. Reagan was returning to his limousine after a speaking engagement when Hinckley shot him with a revolver, seriously wounding him. Hinckley believed the attack would impress the actress Jodie Foster.

‌



View 6 Images Melania Trump appeared to be the first to realise what was unfolding at the dinner (Image: BBC)

It prompted security overhauls at the hotel, including a secured garage designed to fit the presidential limo which leads to a private elevator to ferry the VIPs to a secure suite. It has its own bathroom with monogrammed towels. But despite these changes, a gunman was allowed to enter the hotel on the day of a prestigious event attended by some of the most powerful politicians in the world.

After the latest shooting, Trump said: "I've studied assassinations, and I must tell you, the most impactful people, the people that do the most...The people that make the biggest impact, they're the ones that they go after."

Article continues below

Former FBI agent Jonathan Gilliam said he was astonished that a would-be assassin was again allowed to get so near the President in Saturday's shooting. He said: "There has been better security at events like the Superbowl. You cannot get a bag in, bigger than a purse. I cannot for the life of me understand how this keeps happening."

Fellow former FBI agent Barry Donadio said of the Washington attack: "I have manned check points like that. Watching the video of him running to get through gave me chills. He ran quickly. If they had not stopped him then he would have got right through. They did exactly what they were supposed to do, but that video is terrifying."

News.title: Beatrice and Eugenie's 'despair' over Fergie's tell-all interview as motive questioned
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Beatrice and Eugenie's 'despair' over Fergie's tell-all interview as motive questioned

With sources claiming that the former Duchess of York is considering lucrative deals as an attempt to clear her name, one royal expert believes she will have to weigh up how such an interview would impact her daughters

View 4 Images Sarah Ferguson, and her daughters Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie (Image: PA)

Sarah Ferguson is reportedly weighing up her options after being presented with lucrative offers in exchange for a tell-all interview or TV documentary series. The former Duchess of York has not spoken publicly since being embroiled in the Epstein scandal, although has denied any knowledge of criminal activity after she was repeatedly named in the millions of documents released by the US Department of Justice in relation to the billionaire paedophile’s crimes.

‌



After not being seen in public for over seven months, Fergie was recently snapped at a £2,000-per-night ski chalet in Austria, where she is believed to have been keeping a low profile since her involvement with Epstein became apparent.

‌



View 4 Images Sarah Ferguson has been holed up in an Austrian ski chalet for several months (Image: AP)

‌



In recent weeks, a source told the Mirror that Fergie, who is said to be strapped for cash, is open to giving a tell-all interview about her life, with US streaming execs, as well as several British producers, expressing an interest, with one American bid said to be worth $1.75m (£1.3m).

However, despite the lucrative pay cheque, Sarah is said to be concerned on how such an exposé would impact her daughters, Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie.

The source said: “Sarah knows she needs the money and she’s open to the right television opportunity, but she’s also very aware of the tightrope she’s walking. Her daughters are part of the Royal Family, and anything she does reflects on them.”

‌



They added: “There’s a real sense she wants, in fact needs, to tell her side of the story, but she knows it has to be handled carefully. She can’t ignore the reality of how this looks, especially given Andrew’s close relationship with the paedophile.”

View 4 Images Beatrice and Eugenie would likely be in 'despair' if Fergie speaks out (Image: PA)

While a tell-all has not been confirmed, former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond believes Fergie’s daughters would be inconsolable if she were to share her story, as any interview would likely shine a light on Beatrice and Eugenie’s potential involvement with Epstein, which they have been trying to avoid.

‌



Jennie told the Mirror : “I think her daughters would be in despair if she went ahead with a tell-all interview. Whatever she said would result in headline news and the sort of publicity that Beatrice and Eugenie are desperately trying to avoid.

“If she wants to protect her family, her best strategy is to continue keeping as low a profile as possible. She is obviously angry and hurt by what has happened – although, frankly, she has only herself to blame for continuing her friendship with Epstein, and also lying about having ended it.”

View 4 Images Fergie was named several times in the Epstein files (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

‌



While Jennie said she understands why Fergie would want to sell her story, she believes any tell-all interview would no doubt include stories from behind Palace walls, which would likely to draw a further chasm between the former Duchess and the Royal Family.

Jennie said: “Further revelations would only add fuel to the fire and antagonise the Palace even further. I hope Sarah sees sense and refuses the offers which are said to be coming in, even though I’m sure they are highly lucrative.”

While reports of the tell-all documentary interview are said to stem from Sarah’s need for financial help, the royal expert is not convinced Fergie is as cash-strapped as it has been claimed, given how long she has reportedly been residing in the up-market Austrian ski resort.

‌



“I simply don’t buy the idea that she is desperate for money,” Jennie said. “She really doesn’t have to stay in these extravagant places she seems to be hanging out in at the moment – no doubt relying on the generosity of the friends she still has.”

The royal expert suggested that rather than selling her story to the highest bidder to rehabilitate her public image, she would be better off leaving the ski resort and living by modest means as she adjusts to her life without the help of the Palace purse.

Article continues below

Jennie said: “What’s wrong with renting a modest house wherever she decides to live, being her own woman and cutting her cloth to suit her finances? It’s what the rest of us have to do, and I think she might regain a tiny modicum of respect if she did the same.”

News.title: NINE DAYS THAT SHOOK BRITAIN Inside the General Strike 100 years on as establishment 'bullied' workers
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: NINE DAYS THAT SHOOK BRITAIN Inside the General Strike 100 years on as establishment 'bullied' workers

A general strike took place in the United Kingdom from 4 to 12 May 1926 in an attempt to prevent wage reductions and worsening conditions for 1.2 million locked-out coal miners

View 7 Images Strikers reading the latest news during the General Strike (Image: Getty Images)

On 4 May 1926 the British people woke to a strange quiet. Trains, trams, and buses remained in their depots. The great factory chimneys that usually belched smoke into the air above the nation’s industrial towns were idle. The general strike had begun. For the next nine days, more than 2 million workers - dockers, railwaymen, bus drivers, printers, and factory workers - downed tools. They joined the country’s one million coalminers, who’d been locked out of their pits after refusing to accept swingeing wage cuts.

‌



Britain’s coal owners were a motley collection of aristocrats and businessmen - described by one government minister as ‘the stupidest men in England’. Unwilling to invest in their industry, when times were hard, pay cuts were their solution. British coal was getting less competitive - made worse when Chancellor Winston Churchill returned the pound to the gold standard.

‌



The miners lived hard lives, powering the Empire for little thanks. They wanted pits to be modernised and nationalised. Their leaders included Herbert Smith, a no-nonsense Yorkshireman, who started working in the mines aged ten, and A.J. Cook, a radical firebrand and self-confessed follower of Lenin. Smith saw a friend die underground at 15, while Cook carried a man’s lifeless body home after an accident on his first ever shift. Determined to protect hard-won rights, they coined the slogan ‘not a penny off the pay, not a second on the day’.

‌



7 View 7 Images The General Strike of 1926 lasted nine days and began as a walkout by the coal industry as a result of the fall in domestic coal prices. The rest of Britain's organized labour then joined the strike in sympathy with the miners' cause. (Image: Corbis via Getty Images) 7 View 7 Images 1926: A woman volunteer at the canteen in Hyde Park during the General Strike. (Image: Getty Images)

In the summer of 1925 things reached a head. The miners rejected pay cuts and appealed to the Trades Union Congress (TUC) for help. The TUC agreed to embargo the movement of coal if the miners were locked out. The government caved in, granting a temporary subsidy to keep miners’ wages level. And a Royal Commission chaired by Sir Herbert Samuel would examine the problems in the coal industry.

This temporary victory was dubbed ‘Red Friday’. “You have done it over my blood-stained corpse,” an exasperated Churchill told Cook. The subsidy would only run until the end of April 1926. The stage was set for massive confrontation.

‌



Stanley Baldwin’s Tory government prepared for the clash. Since the Russian revolution of 1917 the establishment had feared communism, reasoning that a national strike could be exploited by revolutionaries to gain power. Hardline Home Secretary William Joynson-Hicks asked: “Is England to be governed by Parliament and the Cabinet or by a handful of trade union leaders?”

But moderate leaders of the TUC and Labour Party were similarly scared of revolution. Jimmy Thomas, the railwaymen’s leader and Labour MP, worked hard to avert the conflict, begging the government to extend negotiations on the eve of the strike. In the early hours of 3 May, printers at the Daily Mail refused to set type for an inflammatory anti-union lead article, giving government hardliners an excuse to break off negotiations. Baldwin shook the hand of TUC secretary Walter Citrine, saying: “I believe if we live we shall meet again to settle it…if we live.” The strike was on.

View 7 Images North East workers demonstrating during the General Strike of May 1926. (Image: Mirrorpix via Getty Images)

‌



With print workers joining the strike, a propaganda war ensued between the unions and the government. Each produced their own daily newspaper. The British Worker pushed the TUC’s line that the strike was a dispute over wages, posing no threat to the constitution. The government’s British Gazette slammed the strike as a revolutionary plot against Britain’s hallowed institutions.

The BBC, then four years old, played a crucial role during the strike, when newspapers were hard to find. Thousands bought wirelesses, to tune into news bulletins. The BBC claimed neutrality, but its information mostly came from government sources. John Reith, its director, even allowed Prime Minister Baldwin to broadcast to the nation from his study. Baldwin said: “I am a man of peace. I am longing and working and praying for peace, but I will not surrender the safety and security of the British Constitution.”

By contrast, when the Archbishop of Canterbury and Opposition party leaders asked to address the public with a compromise proposal, under government pressure, Reith refused. And the BBC and Gazette reported Cardinal Bourne’s sermon decrying the strike as ‘a sin against the obedience which we owe to God.’

‌



View 7 Images 1926: Miners at a Midlands colliery return to work after the General Strike. (Image: Getty Images)

On the ground the strike was more solid than anyone had hoped - or feared. Activists remarked their biggest challenge was keeping those who had not been called out at work. On the third day, a London union official observed: “All the flunkeys in the whole West End of London could blow out all their teeth without getting a ghost of a response from a taxi driver.”

A battle for control commenced between striking workers and the government and its army of middle class volunteers. Strike committees issued permits for the moving of essential supplies. Lorries carried food with signs stating ‘By permission of the TUC’.

‌



Swathes of volunteers signed up to help the government break the strike. Despite high unemployment, hardly any were manual workers, who overwhelmingly supported the unions. Instead, Oxbridge students, encouraged by their colleges, worked on Dover’s docks and drove buses in Hull. At least four passengers and one volunteer were killed due to railway accidents caused by lack of experience. The gentlemen’s clubs of Piccadilly provided units of special constables to help the police. Some volunteers were billeted in bus depots or docked ships, to avoid picket lines. London’s Hyde Park became a giant logistics depot, where society ladies peeled potatoes and made tea for strike-breaking lorry drivers.

View 7 Images Edd Mustill, author of Britain’s Revolutionary Summer - a trade unionist and Labour historian based in Sheffield

As the days passed and more volunteers replaced strikers, ugly scenes erupted. At Tilbury dock, convoys were attacked with stones. In Plymouth, on the day that a team of strikers beat the police 2-1 in a friendly football match, a crowd rioted and attacked trams. Working buses had tyres slashed and engines sabotaged. Most infamously, on 10 May the Flying Scotsman was derailed after a group of miners removed a rail. Remarkably, there was only one injury.

‌



State repression stepped up. Thousands were arrested under emergency regulations giving police sweeping powers. By the strike’s second week, Churchill was readying a paramilitary force, the Civil Constabulary Reserve, to unleash on picket lines.

Union leaders were as worried as the government about the situation spiraling out of control. Almost as soon as the strike began, they explored backchannels for talks - finding a friend in Sir Herbert Samuel, who met Thomas at the London home of a mutual friend. They hammered out a compromise that was enough for the TUC to call off the strike.

View 7 Images Miners’ leaders including Herbert Smith (left) and A.J. Cook (second from right) attend the Samuel Commission. (Image: Supplied)

‌



At noon on 12 May union leaders attended Downing Street to surrender. Immediately, Baldwin made it clear Samuel had been acting alone. The government was not bound to his compromise and had no intention of negotiating. It was too late. The workers were going back. Thousands were victimised. Some could not find work for years.

The miners were left to fight alone for seven long and bitter months. Cook praised the solidarity shown by the workers, but denounced the TUC at a rally 10 days after the strike, saying: “Never have we been bullied by the employers or the Government to the extent that we were bullied by certain trade union leaders to accept a reduction in wages.”

The strike came to be seen as a collective bout of madness - ‘the Nine Days Wonder’ - after which everything returned to normal. Recent pop culture set in the 1920s has either, like Downton Abbey , ignored the strike altogether, or, like Peaky Blinders , reduced the organised working class to a sort of feral gang.

Article continues below

But in the mining areas the strike lived long in people’s memories. Churchill was reportedly still booed in cinemas when he appeared on newsreels, even after the war. A century later, it remains a powerful example, both of working class solidarity and of the lengths to which the establishment will go to protect its power and privilege.

*Britain’s Revolutionary Summer by Edd Mustill - a trade unionist and Labour historian based in Sheffield - is published by Oneworld, priced £16.99.

News.title: 'I paid for friend to come to my Bali wedding and couldn't believe what she did next'
News.content:
'I paid for friend to come to my Bali wedding and couldn't believe what she did next'

A woman has sparked a debate after threatening to take her friend to court following a sticky situation at her destination wedding, and people have shared their own thoughts on it

View Image Many people choose to have destination weddings (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A woman has slammed her friend for not showing up to her destination wedding, leaving her wildly out of pocket. The 25-year-old married her husband, 25, in Bail, Indonesia, in January this year and made sure to foot the expense so her friend's could celebrate with her without worrying about the cost.

‌



She said on Reddit: "It was a destination wedding, but my parents and his parents paid for their own plane tickets and hotel, but we paid for our friends plane tickets and hotel stays. Each plane ticket was about $2,000 (£1,500) and hotel was maybe about $150-300 (£110-£220) for a week."

‌



She went onto explain how her friend, Gemma, brought her newlywed husband, John, along with her, but she made sure to pay for his ticket.

‌



However, when the special day came around, Gemma and John were nowhere to be seen.

She said: " Gemma took the free plane ticket to Bali and the hotel room and when I asked her why she didn’t show up she said that since they couldn’t afford their own honeymoon that this was a perfect opportunity and that Jim decided that he didn’t feel like going.

"I was really hurt by this since Gemma and I have been friends for over 10 years."

‌



Disgusted, the woman has taken to social media to ask users whether she's justified taking her friends to small claims court for the money she spend on plane tickets and the hotel.

In response, one user said: "Can’t believe I’m saying this, but, not the a**hole.

‌



"Someone offers to give you a free vacation on the condition that you attend one party during that time? I’d be jumping for that opportunity.

"To take that free vacation and then no-call-no-show to your friends’ wedding is really shitty behaviour on their part.

"They could have extended their stay if they wanted to treat the trip as their own honeymoon."

‌



Another user added: "I really wish people would stop saying this. Contracts do not have to be formal to be enforced.

"A gift is something given without expectations, so this wasn’t a gift. Oral contracts are considered contracts, at least under US law and many other countries.

"And if there are any texts and emails that say she was buying it with the expectation of her attending the wedding, then a contract would be formed once her friend accepted the ticket and hotel.

‌



"She bought the ticket with the stipulation her friend was coming to the wedding. Her friend didn’t fulfill her end of the contract. Now is she guaranteed to win? No. But she definitely would have a case."

A third user said: "You didn't offer them a gift of a honeymoon. You offered to help them attend your wedding so they didn't have an undue financial burden.

"Also? They could totally have done both, spent some time together in honeymoon mode, and also attended your wedding.

Article continues below

"That they took your money and used it solely for themselves is not okay."

News.title: Washington Hilton Hotel security slammed as 'minimal' over Trump shooting chaos
News.content:
Washington Hilton Hotel security slammed as 'minimal' over Trump shooting chaos

Security at the hotel where a gunman ran towards 'three of the most powerful and important men' in the US has been criticised for being 'minimal' and 'not good'

View 8 Images Trump being shown a magic trick by entertainer moments before shots rang out. (Image: BBC)

A gunman branded a “lone wolf whack job” by Trump charged through 'minimal' security towards a ballroom where “three of the most powerful and important men” in the United States were dining.

‌



It is believed to be the third attempt on President Trump's life in just 21 months, prompting criticisms by experts and fellow guests, stunned by the latest security breach.

‌



Cole Tomas Allen, 31, is believed to have checked in as a guest at the Washington Hilton Hotel, allowing him access to the building. Chillingly it is feared he could have been laying in wait for hours, armed with a shotgun, handgun and 'multiple' knives, as guests and senators held various events throughout the hotel before the glittering event began.

‌



View 8 Images Cole Tomas Allen on the ground after being tackled to the ground (Image: @REALDONALDTRUMP / TRUTH SOCIAL/AFP via Getty Images)

Secret Service agents were forced to tackle the gunman to the ground after he sprinted through their security checkpoint. He had drawn a gun and shot one officer, who was saved by a bullet proof vest.

Allen from Torrance in California, had approached the metal detector at the entrance of the ballroom where 2,500 were attending the annual White House Correspondents’ dinner. He drew a gun and opened fire as he ran towards the packed ballroom. It is believed he fired around four rounds as guests took cover under tables.

‌



Washington’s Metropolitan Police Department interim chief, Jeffery Carroll, said investigators believe that the suspect was staying in the hotel and that appears to be how he was able to enter at the time of the event.

View 8 Images The suspect was caught on surveillance footage sprinting past a security checkpoint and headed straight for the ballroom (Image: TRUTH SOCIAL)

The hotel was closed to the public from 2pm on Saturday ready for the dinner which began at 8pm. The gunman struck around 8.36pm just as the President was being shown a magic trick by the evening’s entertainer.

‌



As shots rang out the top table looked up and the President said he thought it was a ‘tray going down’ while First Lady Melania told him ‘that’s a bad noise’ and they “were whisked away” by heavily armed Secret Service agents with guns drawn.

Sky News’ journalist Mark Stone, who was at the events and had to duck down as shots erupted, said: “It’s a night I don’t think any of us will forget. It was frightening...I heard three or four more pops and I thought ‘no this definitely is a shooting…there were people shouting ‘shots fired’.

View 8 Images Trump appears to duck and then stand before being 'whisked' out of the ballroom (Image: REUTERS)

‌



“It was a very cramped room. He said Agents were climbing over chairs trying to get to other senators who were sat around the round tables after being nvited to join by different media outlets.

He said there were many questions to be answered including: “Was it a mass shooting attempt in a ballroom full of journalists, full of celebrities, congress people, other politicians, policy makers, business people, different groups of people who have enemies?”

He described the security as “not good” adding: “One check just outside the ballroom, no check as we went into the hotel. We were just asked to hold our invitations up…

‌



“It’s a huge hotel and to my knowledge it wasn’t shut to hotel guests but it was shut to the general public…you just had to hold your ticket up and you would be allowed in. There were protests outside, pro-Palestine. It was pouring with rain as well so there was an attempt to get people in.

View 8 Images Secret Service agents sprang into action as shots were fired (Image: Getty Images)

“But if you were already checked in as a hotel guest, you were already inside and that’s kind of chilling actually because it appears that he was, the suspect was checked in as a guest at the hotel which means he was in there the whole time.

‌



“Everyone was there at pre-dinner receptions being hosted by different news organisations in different parts of the hotel before we all went down two floors to the basement to the ballroom area. And it was only there, just outside the ballroom, that the security scanners, airport style and the US Secret Service were checking everyone.

“But it was minimal security, I have to say, for an event where pretty much the whole cabinet were there, as well as the President and the vice President and the speaker of the House. The three most powerful, most important people in the United States, not just in the same building but in the same room.”

Another guest told Sky News, still in his black tie, he thought it was a mass shooting attempt. "I don't think it was an attempted assassination...I think it was an attempted assassination of Americans. Because if he'd wanted to kill the President, he wouldn't be coming through the front. I think his plan was to come through the door and start shooting as many people as possible."

‌



View 8 Images Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (3rd-L) is taken out of the ballroom by security agents (Image: Getty Images)

One witness, claimed she saw the shooter assembling a 'long gun' in a room where bar carts were being stored near the entrance. Helen Mabus said “there was no security” at the time. He was in that room … he grabbed it out of a bag or something adding that the weapon “was long” and “didn’t look like a typical gun”.

“He put it together and … ran towards the stairs to go down to the ballroom,” she said. "It just seems like he was shooting all over the place,” she said, adding that she had heard “at least ten shots”.

‌



But Trump said in an emergency news conference back at the White House praised the brave officers who 'subdued' the gunman and said: “That was very unexpected but incredibly acted upon by Secret Service and law enforcement...

“I don’t care how many people you have, how good they are, you can have the greatest security in history, if you have a whack job who has a brain but it is a little bit distorted, a lot distorted, they can make trouble,” President Trump said at a press conference 30 minutes after the incident."

View 8 Images The alleged shooter is an 'intelligent' tutor and engineer who was educated in an elite college (Image: facebook)

‌



But he described the Washington Hilton was “not a particularly secure building” and used it as an example of why he needed to construct a ballroom at the White House. “This is why we have to have all of the attributes of what we’re planning at the White House. It’s actually a larger room, and it’s much more secure.”

Outside of the same hotel 45 years former President Ronald Reagan was shot and left in critical condition by John Hinckley Jr in 1981.

Law enforcement defended the security with Sean Curran, director of the US Secret Service, saying the incident showed that the agency’s security arrangements “works”.

‌



Allen was not known to security services and was named teacher of the month in December 2024. The honour was announced by C2 Education, which specialises in college ‘test preparation, tutoring and academic advising’.

According to the Los Angeles Times, Dylan Wakayama, president of the Asian American Civic Trust, said Allen tutored several high school students who are members of the organisation, a Torrance-based non-profit.

“They thought he was very intelligent, proficient in biology, mathematics and science. They thought he was on the nicer, quiet side. They were completely shocked when I told them that this all went down,” he said. “I think all of us in Torrance would be shocked if this is the man who attempted to kill the president of the United States,” he said.

‌



View 8 Images Allen graduated from university (Image: FACEBOOK)

Jason Moses told how he helped him with his physics homework: "He was just a pretty normal guy. He was a smart guy. He was a little quirky but you would definitely not have expected him to do the things he did tonight. You'd never expect it, coming from this guy.".

In addition to his part-time work at C2 Education, he’s also self-employed, according to his LinkedIn, identifying as an “indie game developer.”

Article continues below

Cole Allen, who is registered to vote with no party preference, graduated from CalTech in 2017 with a degree in mechanical engineering. While at CalTech, he was a member of the school’s Christian fellowship and the nerf club, according to his LinkedIn profile.

On his profile he describes himself as a game developer, engineer, scientist and teacher. He registered a trademark in 2019 for “Bohrdom” which is a fighting game he created and released on Steam, an online game platform.

News.title: Sabastian Sawe breaks two-hour barrier to make history at London Marathon
News.content:
Sabastian Sawe made history at the London Marathon by becoming the first athlete to run a sub-two-hour marathon in a competitive race.

The 30-year-old Kenyan crossed the line to win in one hour 59 minutes 30 seconds, more than one minute faster than the late Kelvin Kiptum's previous record of 2:00:35, set in 2023.

The great Eliud Kipchoge became the first man to run a marathon in under two hours in 2019, but that was not record-eligible as it was held under controlled conditions.

Already on world record pace as he crossed the halfway mark in 1:00:29, Sawe was able to speed up over the second half of the race to run even faster than Kipchoge's time.

Sawe made his decisive move before the final 10km, with only debutant Yomif Kejelcha able to cover his surge off the front.

Remarkably, Kejelcha became the second man to run under two hours in race conditions, finishing runner-up in 1:59:41.

Half marathon world record holder Jacob Kiplimo also crossed the line faster than Kiptum's former record, completing the podium in 2:00:28.

Sawe, speaking on BBC TV, said: "I am feeling good. I am so happy. It is a day to remember for me."

"We started the race well. Approaching finishing the race, I was feeling strong. Finally reaching the finish line, I saw the time, and I was so excited."
